solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Country song about surrounding country (7)

indicatorNotes.about: turning about sends AIR back to front
indicatorNotes.surrounding: RIA goes around the second country

blocks.note: an air is a tune or song
the Gulf state; this second country is the one RIA surrounds

annotation.surface: A folk song celebrating some neighbouring nation.
annotation.walkthrough: Two countries in one clue: the first 'Country' is the definition, the second is OMAN, which sits inside the reversed song.
annotation.definitionFit: Romania is a country in south-eastern Europe.

entries.clue: More sensitive, overturned Duke’s compensation (6)

indicatorNotes.overturned: in a down clue, turning RAWER over writes it bottom to top

blocks.note: a raw nerve is a sensitive one
D is the abbreviation for Duke, as in peerage lists; the apostrophe-s reads as "has", joining it on

annotation.surface: A touchy duke, toppled from power, claims a payout.
annotation.walkthrough: The comma splits 'More sensitive, overturned' from the duke; it is the sensitivity that gets overturned, not the Duke.
annotation.definitionFit: A reward is something given as compensation for effort or loss.

entries.clue: Mother supported by arthritic dog (7)

indicatorNotes.supported by: in a down clue MA sits on top of STIFF

annotation.surface: An elderly mother leans on her old, arthritic dog.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Arthritic' looks like it describes the dog, but it is its own piece of wordplay; the dog is the plain definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A mastiff is a large, powerful breed of dog.

entries.clue: Suggests friendless Billy drinks at home (9)

indicatorNotes.drinks: NO MATES takes IN inside it, as a drinker takes in drink

blocks.note: Billy No-Mates is British slang for a person with no friends

annotation.surface: A lonely man called Billy drinks by himself at home.
annotation.walkthrough: Billy No-Mates is the British nickname for someone without friends, so 'friendless Billy' drops 'Billy' and gives NO MATES.
annotation.definitionFit: To nominate someone is to suggest them for a post or award.

entries.clue: Outbreak in London borough announced locally (4)

indicatorNotes.announced locally: said as a Londoner says it, dropping the H

blocks.note: Hackney, with the H dropped in Cockney speech

annotation.surface: News of a disease outbreak in one London district, told in the local dialect.
annotation.walkthrough: Hackney is a borough of east London; Cockneys traditionally drop the H, so 'locally' it comes out as 'ACKNEY, which sounds like ACNE.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: acne comes up as a sudden eruption of spots, so an outbreak.

entries.clue: After reflection, get a repository to store work (7)

indicatorNotes.After reflection: the hidden letters are read in a mirror, back to front
indicatorNotes.to store: the words hold the answer inside them

blocks.note: the letters run across the words from the end of "get" into the start of "repository"; read them backwards

annotation.surface: Once you've thought it over, find a place to keep your work.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Repository' makes a coder think of a repo, and that is exactly where the answer hides, backwards across 'get a repository'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a machine that works is said to operate.

entries.clue: Go faster than stalling bikers when half-cut in far-off place (5,5)

indicatorNotes.stalling: OUTPACE stalls ERS, holding it in
indicatorNotes.half-cut: only half of BIKERS is kept

blocks.note: to outpace is to go faster than
BIKERS loses its first half, BIK

annotation.surface: Drunken motorcyclists stall and are overtaken on the way to some remote spot.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Half-cut' is British slang for drunk, which suits the bikers, but here it simply halves the word.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by description: the space beyond Earth's atmosphere is as far-off a place as there is.

entries.clue: Centre of Great Lake is scary (5)

indicatorNotes.Centre of: takes the middle letter of GREAT

blocks.note: Lake Erie, one of the Great Lakes

annotation.surface: The middle of one of North America's Great Lakes is a frightening place.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Great Lake' reads as one phrase pointing to ERIE, but 'Great' is only there to give up its central E.
annotation.definitionFit: Eerie means strange and frightening.

entries.clue: Wonderful gallery is overhead (7)

blocks.note: the Tate is the London art gallery

annotation.surface: Someone praises a gallery with an impressive ceiling.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Overhead' is a noun here: an acetate is the clear sheet laid on an overhead projector, often itself called an overhead.
annotation.definitionFit: An overhead is a transparency for an overhead projector, made of acetate film.
annotation.definitionNote: overhead is used as a noun, the transparency

entries.clue: Judge ties up partner (8)

indicatorNotes.up: "up" as in "stirred up" or "mixed up": TIES is churned so its letters come out in a new order

annotation.surface: A magistrate binds up a companion.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Judge' is a verb, not the person in the wig: to judge a distance is to estimate it.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the verb: to judge a height by eye is to estimate it.

entries.clue: Women’s interests unfortunately blocked by male in parliament (11)

indicatorNotes.blocked by: M is lodged inside the rearranged letters

blocks.note: W is the standard abbreviation for women (as on toilet doors); the apostrophe-s reads as "has", joining it on

annotation.surface: Women's concerns are sadly obstructed by a man in the legislature.
annotation.walkthrough: Westminster is used as a name for the UK Parliament, after the district of London where it sits.
annotation.definitionFit: A metonym: the London district where the Houses of Parliament stand is used as a name for Parliament itself.

entries.clue: Put away jumper having removed two coats (3)

indicatorNotes.having removed two coats: the outer two layers of letters come off each end of SWEATER

blocks.note: a jumper is the British word for a sweater; two letters come off each end

annotation.surface: Someone takes off two layers and stows their sweater.
annotation.walkthrough: A jumper is the British word for a sweater. Each 'coat' is one letter at each end, so two coats strip SW and ER.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: to put away a big meal is to eat it all.

entries.clue: Singer breaks rules (6)

indicatorNotes.breaks: SINGER is broken up and rearranged

annotation.surface: A vocalist flouts the regulations.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rules' looks like a plural noun beside 'breaks', but it is a verb: the monarch rules, or reigns.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the verb: a monarch who rules a country reigns over it.

entries.clue: Regularly targeted by FA, Roberto Mancini originally managed Forest (4,4)

indicatorNotes.Regularly: takes every other letter of TARGETED
indicatorNotes.originally: takes the first letters of Roberto and Mancini

blocks.note: the initials of the football manager

annotation.surface: A football story: the FA keeps going after Roberto Mancini, who once managed Nottingham Forest.
annotation.walkthrough: Nottingham Forest is an English football club, so 'managed Forest' reads as a job; here Forest is the definition, a stand of planted trees.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a plantation of trees grown for timber is a managed forest.

entries.clue: Discontinuing accomplished mischief-making? (10)

blocks.note: a pro is accomplished, a professional

annotation.surface: Someone skilled at causing trouble is asked to stop.
annotation.walkthrough: To prorogue Parliament is to discontinue its session without dissolving it.
annotation.definitionFit: Proroguing a parliament discontinues its sittings.

entries.clue: Tense optimist’s view? (6,7)

annotation.surface: An anxious optimist looks ahead.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tense' looks like an adjective describing the optimist, but it is the grammar noun: the future perfect is the tense of 'I will have done'.
annotation.definitionFit: The future perfect is a verb tense; an optimist also sees a perfect future.

blocks.note: a grammatical tense, as in 'I will have finished'
an optimist expects everything ahead to be perfect

entries.clue: Republican drops in on President for collection of pipes? (4,5)

indicatorNotes.drops in: in a down clue the R of ERDOGAN drops lower down into the word

blocks.note: Recep Tayyip Erdoğan, President of Turkey; take out its R
R = Republican, dropped back in two places lower

annotation.surface: A Republican drops in on the President to look at some pipes.
annotation.walkthrough: The R already in ERDOGAN slides down: ERDOGAN becomes EDORGAN. The question mark flags the definition: a reed organ's reeds are, loosely, a collection of pipes.
annotation.definitionFit: A reed organ, such as a harmonium, sounds by reeds, which are a kind of pipe.

entries.clue: In general, answer was recalled with difficulty (2,1,5)

indicatorNotes.recalled: called back, so WAS is read backwards

annotation.surface: Broadly speaking, the answer was hard to remember.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Recalled' pretends to mean remembered; here it only sends WAS back the other way.
annotation.definitionFit: As a whole means taken all together, in general.

entries.clue: What fraud investigators aim to do for proceedings in court (6,7)

annotation.definition: What fraud investigators aim to do
annotation.surface: Investigators pursue fraudsters through the legal system.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Court' suggests a law court; it is a squash court, and the rackets are what you play with there.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: crushing criminal schemes, and the equipment for a game played on a squash court.

blocks.clueFragment: What fraud investigators aim to do
blocks.note: to squash is to crush; rackets are criminal scams
the bats used in the game of squash, played on a court

entries.clue: Universal acclaim for lift (7)

annotation.surface: Everyone applauds a lift.
annotation.walkthrough: U is the British film certificate meaning suitable for all, hence universal.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain, rather literary synonym: to raise something up.

entries.clue: Weapon is flipping expensive on 5th of November (7)

indicatorNotes.flipping: to flip something is to turn it over, so IS is read back to front
indicatorNotes.5th of: takes the fifth letter of November

annotation.surface: Fireworks for Bonfire Night cost a ridiculous amount.
annotation.walkthrough: The 5th of November is Bonfire Night in Britain, and 'flipping' looks like a mild British oath before 'expensive'; both are just instructions.
annotation.definitionFit: A sidearm is a weapon worn at the side, such as a pistol.

entries.clue: Lean on body part (6)

blocks.note: to lean towards something is to tend towards it

annotation.surface: Rest your weight on part of your body.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lean' looks like the adjective for a fit body; it is the verb, to incline or tend.
annotation.definitionFit: A tendon is a part of the body joining muscle to bone.

entries.clue: African natives fight unruly Goths (8)

indicatorNotes.unruly: unruly means refusing to stay in line, so the letters of GOTHS break ranks into a new order

annotation.surface: Local tribesmen take on a band of barbarian Goths.
annotation.walkthrough: 'African natives' suggests people, but the natives are animals: warthogs are wild pigs native to Africa.
annotation.definitionFit: Warthogs are wild pigs native to Africa.

entries.clue: Large animal in river (5)

annotation.surface: A big beast wallowing in the water.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In' reads as a link telling you where the animal is, but it is the wordplay: in = HIP. The hippo really does live in rivers.
annotation.definitionFit: The hippopotamus is a very large African animal.

entries.clue: Draw lots, briefly, to follow leader in Denmark (6)

indicatorNotes.briefly: OODLES is cut short by its last letter

annotation.surface: Drawing lots to decide who leads Denmark.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Draw lots' is a fixed phrase for a raffle; split it, and Draw is the definition while lots gives OODLES.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym by example: idle scribbling in a margin is a way to draw.

entries.clue: Manager is stud (4)

annotation.surface: The man in charge is a ladies' man.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stud' reads as a lothario; it is a raised knob or ornament, which is also a boss.
annotation.definitionFit: A boss is a manager, and also a round stud on a shield or ceiling.

blocks.note: the person in charge at work
a raised knob, as on a shield or a vaulted ceiling

entries.clue: Charm bird removing clothing (3)

indicatorNotes.removing clothing: strips the outer letters off ROBIN, as clothes are the outside layer

blocks.note: the robin; take off its outer R and N

annotation.surface: An undressed bird is somehow charming.
annotation.walkthrough: Obi (or obeah) is a West Indian folk magic, and the word also means a charm or fetish used in it.
annotation.definitionFit: An obi is a charm or amulet in obeah magic.

entries.clue: Lad snooping around toxic chemical storage facility (6,5)

indicatorNotes.around: LAD SNOOPING is turned around into a new order

annotation.surface: A boy pokes about a plant where toxic chemicals are stored.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition sounds industrial, but the 'facility' is in an animal's body: a snake's poison gland stores its venom.
annotation.definitionFit: A poison gland secretes and holds venom in an animal.

entries.clue: Soon, entrepreneur on vacation will meet presidential adviser, once head of government (7)

indicatorNotes.on vacation: ENTREPRENEUR is emptied, leaving its outer letters
indicatorNotes.once head of: takes the first letter of government

blocks.note: Elon Musk, who advised President Trump

annotation.surface: A businessman back from holiday is soon to meet a former head of state's adviser.
annotation.walkthrough: The entrepreneur and the presidential adviser look like the same man, and he is: Elon Musk. But only ELON counts; the entrepreneur gives just its ends.
annotation.definitionFit: An archaism: ere means before, so ere long is before long, meaning soon.

entries.clue: He puts people out with article on kinky sex (7)

annotation.surface: A bouncer ejects customers over an article about kinky sex.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Puts people out' sounds like throwing them out or annoying them; the Sandman of folklore puts people out by sending them to sleep.
annotation.definitionFit: The Sandman is the folk figure who sends people to sleep.
